mainTopic: The last two of the few disputes where the הלכה follows ריש לקיש against רבי יוחנן: wording a gift to each heir, and a son who sells property his father gave him with the father keeping its use until death.
overview: The גמרא finishes its list of cases where the הלכה follows ריש לקיש against רבי יוחנן. In the first case, a man dividing his property among his heirs must use the gift wording for each heir. In the second, a father writes his property to his son 'after his death,' and the son sells it and then dies before the father. רבי יוחנן says the buyer gets nothing, because owning the use (קנין פירות) is like owning the thing itself. ריש לקיש says the buyer acquires. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about a יבם who married his pregnant יבמה. רבי אליעזר says that even if the baby was not viable, he must divorce her. רבא links this to רבי מאיר's penalty for marrying a pregnant or nursing woman, and אביי shows two ways the two rulings could differ. רבא adds that even the חכמים require a real גט, and מר זוטרא proves this from the wording. Finally, a baby who dies within thirty days is a doubt, and two students report רבא differently on whether its remarried mother must do חליצה if her new husband is a כהן. רבינא's challenge to רב משרשיא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the gift wording must be said for each heir
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that when someone divides his property among heirs, the division only works if he says for each person that he is giving it 'as a gift.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: they never acquire until he says, 'So-and-so and so-and-so shall inherit such-and-such field and such-and-such field, which I have given them as a gift, and they shall inherit them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes stating ריש לקיש's side of a dispute with רבי יוחנן about how a person dividing his estate must word it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person may give one heir more and another less only by using the language of a gift (מתנה). ריש לקיש holds that saying 'gift' for one heir is not enough; it must cover each heir by name and field. This is one of the cases in the גמרא's list where the הלכה follows ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: He never acquires; the transfer does not take effect
So-and-so; a placeholder for a person's name

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how carefully a person must phrase a division of property for it to work against the Torah's normal rules of inheritance.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
They never acquire
until he says:
"So-and-so and so-and-so shall inherit
such-and-such field and such-and-such field
which I have given them as a gift,
and they shall inherit them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the dispute begun before this section, giving ריש לקיש's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A division of an estate among heirs takes effect only if the gift wording is said for each heir.

steps.title: The last case: a father who writes his property to his son after his death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces the last case in the list by quoting a משנה: when a father writes all his property to his son 'after his death,' neither father nor son can sell it outright.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other case is what we learned in a משנה: One who writes all his property to his son 'after his death' — the father cannot sell, because he gave it to the son; and the son cannot sell, because it is in the father's control. If the father sold, it is sold until he dies. If the son sold, the buyer has nothing until the father dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case on its list and first quotes the background משנה. It is setting up the dispute that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ownership is split: the son owns the property itself, but the father keeps the right to use it and its produce for life. So the father can only sell his right of use until he dies. If the son sells, the buyer gets nothing while the father is alive.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one; the next case on the list

steps.confusionAlert: 'After his death' does not mean the gift only starts when the father dies. The son already owns the property now; only the use stays with the father until he dies.

phrases.english: And the other one is what we learned in a mishna:
One who writes all his property to his son
after his death,
phrases.notes: The son gets the property now, but the father keeps the use of it until he dies.

phrases.english: the father cannot sell,
because he gave them to the son,
and the son cannot sell,
because they are in the father's control.

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר הָאָב — מְכוּרִין עַד שֶׁיָּמוּת הוּא,
phrases.english: If the father sold, they are sold until he dies;
if the son sold,
the buyer has nothing
until the father dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the previous case on the list to the last one, starting with its background משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When property is written to a son 'after death,' the father keeps use for life and the son owns the property; neither can sell it fully.

steps.title: The dispute: the son sold and then died before his father
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about a son who sold the property and then died while his father was still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was stated: The son sold during the father's lifetime, and the son died during the father's lifetime. רבי יוחנן said: the buyer did not acquire. ריש לקיש said: the buyer did acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the actual argument between the אמוראים about a case the משנה did not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the son's buyer waits until the father dies. But here the son died first, so the son never got the use of the property while he was alive. רבי יוחנן says the sale fails completely; ריש לקיש says the buyer gets the property once the father dies.

phrases.english: And it was stated:
The son sold during the father's lifetime,
and the son died during the father's lifetime.
phrases.notes: Afterward the father dies too; the question is whether the buyer gets the property then.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לֹא קָנָה לוֹקֵחַ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: The buyer did not acquire,
and Reish Lakish said: The buyer did acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the משנה's case one step further, to a situation the משנה did not address.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: the buyer gets nothing. ריש לקיש: the buyer acquires.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reason: owning the use is like owning the thing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's reason is that קנין פירות is like קנין הגוף, so the father counts as the real owner while alive, and the son never owned anything he could sell.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said the buyer did not acquire because owning the produce is like owning the item itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the father holds the right to use the property, he counts as its owner as long as he lives. The son would only become the true owner at the father's death. Since the son died first, he never owned it, so his sale never had anything to take effect on.

keyTerms.meaning: Ownership of the produce; the right to use something and its yield

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן holds קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי: whoever owns the use of the property counts as its owner, so a son who dies before his father never owned anything he could sell.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule קנין פירות כקנין הגוף is a basic idea that shows up in many places in ש״ס.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר לֹא קָנָה לוֹקֵחַ —
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said the buyer did not acquire,
because ownership of the produce
phrases.notes: The father's right to use the property and eat its crops for his whole life.

phrases.english: is like ownership of the item itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר לֹא קָנָה לוֹקֵחַ — קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רבי יוחנן's side of the dispute in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי: owning the use is like owning the item itself.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the buyer does acquire
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that the buyer did acquire the property. Owning the produce is not like owning the item itself, so the son really owned it and could sell it.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: the buyer acquired it, because owning the use of something is not the same as owning the thing itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives ריש לקיש's side of the argument from Step 3, together with his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that the father's right to the produce makes him the real owner. ריש לקיש disagrees: the father only has the use of the property, while the son owns the property itself. So the son's sale works. The buyer just has to wait until the father dies before he can use it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is not like / is not the same as

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says owning the produce is like owning the item, so the sale fails. ריש לקיש says it is not, so the sale works.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
The buyer did acquire it.
Ownership of the produce is not
the same as ownership of the item itself.
phrases.notes: The father keeps the produce, but the son owns the property itself, so the son's sale counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the argument and its reason, matching רבי יוחנן's reason in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The buyer acquires the property, because owning the produce is not the same as owning the item itself.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי אליעזר says he must divorce her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's case of a pregnant יבמה whose child was not viable. A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר saying the יבם must divorce her with a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If the child is not viable, etc.' A ברייתא taught: in the name of רבי אליעזר they said, he must send her away with a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה, then brings a ברייתא that disagrees with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the משנה, if the baby turns out not to be viable, the יבום counted and he may stay married to her. רבי אליעזר says he must still divorce her. At the time of the יבום he was not allowed to do it, because she was pregnant.

keyTerms.meaning: A viable child, one who will live
He must send her out with a bill of divorce

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not say the יבום failed. He agrees it worked. He only says the man must divorce her because he did it at a time when it was forbidden.

phrases.english: "If the child is not viable, etc."
phrases.notes: The גמרא is jumping back to the משנה about a יבם who married a pregnant יבמה. 'כו׳' just means 'and so on.'

phrases.english: It was taught:
In the name of Rabbi Eliezer they said:
He must send her out with a bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין הַוָּלָד שֶׁל קַיָּימָא כּוּ׳. תָּנָא: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the property argument and goes back to an earlier line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, a יבם who did יבום with a pregnant יבמה must divorce her, even if the child turns out not to be viable.

steps.title: רבא: רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר hold the same idea
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר share one idea. רבי אליעזר's version is the ruling just quoted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר said the same thing. רבי אליעזר's version is what we just said.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא links רבי אליעזר's ruling to a ruling of רבי מאיר. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא shows us רבי מאיר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared idea is a penalty. If a man marries a woman while he is not allowed to, he must divorce her, even if the reason for the ban later goes away. רבא points to רבי אליעזר's ruling first and leaves רבי מאיר's for the next step.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Eliezer
said one and the same thing.
Rabbi Eliezer: this ruling that we just said.
phrases.notes: He means רבי אליעזר's ruling from the ברייתא right before: the יבם must divorce her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי אליעזר's ruling and links it to a ruling of רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר share one idea: a forbidden marriage must end in divorce, even after the reason for the ban is gone.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's ruling: a pregnant or nursing woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי מאיר's ruling. A man who married a woman pregnant from, or nursing the baby of, another man must divorce her and may never take her back. The חכמים say he may remarry her once the waiting time is over.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: a man may not marry a woman who is pregnant from another man, or who is nursing another man's baby. If he did marry her, he must divorce her and may never take her back. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: he must divorce her, and when the time comes when he is allowed to marry her, he may marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's point by quoting the ברייתא where רבי מאיר gives his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too, the ban (pregnant or nursing) is only for a limited time. Still, רבי מאיר says that once the man broke it, he may never take her back, even after the time passes. That is the same idea as רבי אליעזר's: a penalty that lasts even after the reason is gone. The חכמים disagree and allow him to remarry her later.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman pregnant from another man
A woman nursing another man's baby
He may never take her back

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר both say: marrying when it was not allowed brings a penalty of divorce, even after the problem goes away. The חכמים are more lenient.
steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים also say he must divorce her now. They only argue about whether he may remarry her later.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a shared idea behind two separate rulings: a penalty for breaking a ban, not a claim that the marriage itself failed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir: as it is taught in a ברייתא:
A man may not marry a woman pregnant from another man,
nor a woman nursing another man's baby.
And if he did marry her,
he must divorce her and may never take her back;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say: he must divorce her,
and when the time comes when he may marry her,
phrases.notes: That means once the baby is old enough that the ban no longer applies.

phrases.english: he may marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי מאיר's side of רבא's comparison.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that רבי מאיר holds the same idea as רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי מאיר rules that a man who married a woman pregnant from, or nursing the baby of, another man may never take her back.

steps.title: אביי: Maybe רבי אליעזר is strict only because of a Torah prohibition
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that רבי אליעזר may be strict only in the יבמה case, which risks a Torah prohibition. In רבי מאיר's case, which is only rabbinic, רבי אליעזר may agree with the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: How do you know? Maybe they don't agree. Maybe רבי אליעזר says this only here, because the יבם runs into the Torah prohibition of a brother's wife. But there, where the prohibition is only rabbinic, he may hold like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions רבא's claim that רבי אליעזר and רבי מאיר share one idea. He shows that רבי אליעזר's strict ruling could have a reason that does not apply to רבי מאיר's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the יבמה case, if the baby turns out to be viable, the יבם has been with his brother's wife, which is a Torah prohibition. Marrying another man's pregnant or nursing wife is only rabbinic. So רבי אליעזר's strictness may come from the Torah-level danger, and he could still agree with the lenient חכמים in the rabbinic case.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do you know?
A brother's wife, forbidden by the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: 'Here' (הָכָא) means the יבמה case of רבי אליעזר, and 'there' (הָתָם) means רבי מאיר's case of the pregnant or nursing woman. Keep the two straight.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: From where do you know this?
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבא, who said the two תנאים share one idea.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is not so,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָכָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says his ruling only here,
because he runs into
the Torah prohibition of a brother's wife,
phrases.notes: If the baby is viable, there was never a יבום, so she stays simply his brother's wife.

phrases.english: but there, where it is only rabbinic,
he holds like the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא לָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's linking of the rulings in steps 6-8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's claim that רבי אליעזר and רבי מאיר share one idea
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר's case involves a Torah prohibition and רבי מאיר's case is only rabbinic, so רבי אליעזר's strictness need not carry over

steps.title: אביי: Maybe רבי מאיר is strict only because it is a rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: אביי's second option: רבי מאיר may be strict only because rabbinic laws sometimes get extra protection. In the Torah-level יבמה case, people stay away on their own, so רבי מאיר might not demand a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else: רבי מאיר says this only there, because it is rabbinic, and the חכמים made their own words stronger than Torah words. But here, where it is a Torah law, people stay away from it anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second way to separate the two opinions, this time from רבי מאיר's side. He shows that רבי מאיר's strictness may also have a reason that does not reach רבי אליעזר's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes the Sages protect their own rules extra strongly so people will not treat them lightly. A Torah prohibition does not need that extra fence, because people already keep far from it. So רבי מאיר could be strict in the rabbinic case and still not require a גט in the יבמה case.
steps.confusionAlert: This sounds backwards: the rabbinic law is treated more strictly than the Torah law. The point is that people already respect Torah laws, so only the rabbinic law needs extra protection.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי gives two separate reasons why רבי אליעזר and רבי מאיר might not share one idea. The difference is that one case involves a Torah prohibition and the other only a rabbinic one.

phrases.english: Alternatively:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says his ruling only there,
because it is a rabbinic law,
and the Sages strengthened their own words
more than those of the Torah,
but here, where it is from the Torah,
people surely keep away from it.
phrases.notes: So there is no need for an extra penalty like a forced גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel rejection of רבא's linking, now from רבי מאיר's side
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's claim that the two rulings share one idea
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי מאיר's strictness may come from extra protection given to rabbinic laws, which a Torah-level case does not need

steps.title: רבא: The חכמים also require a גט
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that when the חכמים say the man must send out the pregnant or nursing woman, they mean with a real גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And even according to the חכמים, he must send her out with a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא returns to the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים and explains the חכמים's opinion. Even the lenient חכמים require a full divorce, not just separating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים argued with רבי מאיר only about whether the man may remarry her later. רבא makes clear that they agree he must give a גט now. The disagreement is about the future, not about how to end the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to the words of the Sages
He must send her out with a bill of divorce

phrases.english: Rava said: And according to the words of the Sages:
phrases.notes: These are the חכמים who argue with רבי מאיר in step 8.

phrases.english: He must send her out with a bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, וּלְדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים: יוֹצִיאָהּ בְּגֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves אביי's challenge and clarifies the חכמים's position from step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to the חכמים, the man must divorce the pregnant or nursing woman with a גט

steps.title: מר זוטרא: The wording 'יוציא' proves רבא right
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא supports רבא from the חכמים's exact word: they said 'send out', not 'separate', which means a real divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: The wording shows this too, because it teaches 'he must send out' and not 'he must separate'. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא brings a proof for רבא from the precise words the חכמים used. The גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יוציא' (send out) is the normal word for divorcing with a גט. If the חכמים meant only staying apart, they would have said 'יפריש' (separate). Their choice of word shows they meant a full divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; it is proven

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said: The wording is also precise,
since it teaches: 'He must send out,'
and it does not teach: 'He must separate.'
Learn from this.

steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the חכמים require a גט
steps.raayaSupportSource: The חכמים's use of the word 'יוציא' rather than 'יפריש'
steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי מאיר and the חכמים require a גט. They argue only about whether he may remarry her later.

steps.title: רב אשי quotes: A baby who lives thirty days is not a נפל
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a baby who lives thirty days is not a נפל. From this he infers that a baby who dies earlier is a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב הושעיא בריה דרב אידי: We learned there that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Any human who lives thirty days is not a נפל. So if it did not live that long, it is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי opens a new discussion by quoting a teaching about when a baby counts as viable. This sets up the case and the dispute that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living thirty days proves the baby was viable, not a נפל. The inference is that a baby who dies before thirty days is uncertain: it may or may not have been viable. This doubt matters for whether the father's widow needs יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: There we learned (a teaching from elsewhere)
A baby not able to live; a stillbirth

steps.whyThisMatters: If a baby who died early is a doubt, the widow's status is also unclear, so it affects whether she needs יבום or חליצה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Hoshaya, son of Rav Idi:
We learned there,
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Any human baby that lives thirty days
is not a stillbirth.
So if it did not live that long, it is a doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: הָתָם תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic about how to know whether a baby was viable
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A baby who lives thirty days is not a נפל; one who dies before that is a doubt

steps.title: A woman who remarried after the baby died: the rule depends on whom she married
steps.stepSummary: The baby died within thirty days and the mother went ahead and got engaged to another man. רבינא, quoting רבא, says she does חליצה if she married a ישראל, but not if she married a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if the baby died within thirty days, and the mother went ahead and became engaged to another man, רבינא said in the name of רבא: If she is now the wife of a ישראל, she does חליצה. If she is the wife of a כהן, she does not do חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a case built on רב אשי's point that a baby who dies within thirty days is a doubt. It gives the first opinion about what to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby was a נפל, the husband really died childless, so his brother's link to her (יבום) still applies and she needs חליצה. For a ישראל's wife, חליצה is just an extra safety step, and she can stay married. A woman who did חליצה is forbidden to a כהן, so in that case רבא does not require חליצה. That way the doubt does not break up her marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: She became engaged (קידושין) to a man
In the name of (quoting a teacher)
She does חליצה (the ceremony that releases her from the brother-in-law)

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying a כהן's wife is never a יבמה. The doubt is the same in both cases. He is only saying that the חליצה step is not required when it would ruin her marriage to a כהן.

phrases.english: And it was stated: if [the baby] died within thirty days,
phrases.notes: This is the baby from רב אשי's point just before: the only child the dead husband left.

phrases.english: and she went ahead and became engaged [to another man],
Ravina said in the name of Rava:
If she is the wife of a regular Jew, she does חליצה,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵשֶׁת כֹּהֵן הִיא — אֵינָהּ חוֹלֶצֶת.
phrases.english: but if she is the wife of a כהן, she does not do חליצה.
phrases.notes: A woman who did חליצה is forbidden to a כהן, so חליצה here would end her new marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב אשי's point that a baby who dies within thirty days is a doubt, and applies it to a widow who already remarried.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ישראל's wife does חליצה because of the doubt. A כהן's wife does not, so that her marriage is not broken up.

steps.title: A second report of רבא: she does חליצה either way
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא reports רבא differently: both the ישראל's wife and the כהן's wife do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said in the name of רבא: Both this one and that one do חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: A different student reports רבא's opinion differently. In his version, the new husband's status makes no difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the doubt about the baby is taken seriously even when it costs her the marriage. A כהן's wife must also do חליצה, even though she then becomes forbidden to him. So the two students disagree only about the כהן's wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one (the same rule for both cases)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the debate in the coming lines: may the חכמים set aside a doubtful יבום link to protect a marriage to a כהן?

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said in the name of Rava:
Both this woman and that woman do חליצה.
phrases.notes: Meaning the ישראל's wife and also the כהן's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different report of רבא that disagrees with רבינא's version about the כהן's wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every such woman does חליצה, even the wife of a כהן.

steps.title: רבינא turns to challenge רב משרשיא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא starts speaking to רב משרשיא. His actual words come in the next lines.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready for רבינא to question רב משרשיא's version of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is said yet. The opening tells us the two students will now argue over which report of רבא is correct, and the argument centers on the כהן's wife.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Mesharshiyya:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רבינא's response to רב משרשיא's different report of רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב משרשיא's version, that even a כהן's wife does חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The content of the challenge comes in the next lines. This line only opens the exchange.
